lens: statistics/methodology (does census design support the claim)
central_claim: Because this document enumerates the whole modality space first and grades second (unlike three prior keyword searches), its verdict counts and its named 'live residue' of 31 candidate classes are an audited denominator that can be trusted where a search's silence could not.

blockers.summary: The headline verdict table in §2 and the '31 classes survive' claim that opens §3 do not match systems/graph/modalities.json — the file the document's own frontmatter says owns these rows — at the identical pinned commit. Actual: 20 candidate / 95 excluded. Claimed: 31 candidate / 84 excluded. That is an 11-class discrepancy in exactly the count §1 calls 'the whole methodological claim of this document' (a denominator that a checker can verify).
blockers.evidence: Doc §2 table (lines 59-68): '✑ excluded ... 84 ... 83' and '⭑ candidate ... 31 ... 9', repeated at line 321 ('Eighty-four classes are closed here on first inspection'). Recomputed directly from `git show ad87aa4c7c40729de3e8bc2d7f6e9fe3835415b4:systems/graph/modalities.json` (217 rows): Counter({'excluded': 95, 'on_board': 41, 'already_rejected': 33, 'candidate': 20, 'not_applicable': 11, 'parked_capability': 9, 'in_clinical_use': 8}). The generated view at the same commit, `git show ad87aa4c7c40729de3e8bc2d7f6e9fe3835415b4:systems/views/modality-census.md`, agrees with the graph, not with the manuscript: 'candidate | 20 | 6' / 'excluded | 95 | 86' / '14 of the 111 are live' (the manuscript says 18). So the graph and its own regenerated view are mutually consistent; only the manuscript's typed table diverges from both, at the same commit.
blockers.fix: Stop hand-typing the §2 table and the '31'/'84'/'18' figures in §3's opening sentence. Derive them from systems/graph/modalities.json (or quote systems/views/modality-census.md verbatim) as CLAUDE.md §1 already requires for every total in this repository, then re-run §3's per-theme review below to remove the classes that no longer belong there.

blockers.summary: At least six specific classes are narrated in §3 as part of the surviving 31 ('The live residue... Thirty-one classes survive... every one of them is registered as a route') with no closure noted, while systems/graph/modalities.json records verdict=excluded for every one of them, several explicitly re-graded and closed on 2026-08-09 — the document's own date — with rationale text reading 'This closes the class.' One instance (matrix biosynthesis) is a direct self-contradiction within the manuscript itself: §3.4 asserts the class has never been graded, and §3.8, later in the same document, reports the graded result.
blockers.evidence: (1) Transcriptional CDK inhibition — doc §3.1 (line 146-153) presents it as narrower-but-'still worth a route'. MOD-TRANSCRIPTIONAL-CDK verdict='excluded', rationale: '⛔ RE-GRADED 2026-08-09, the same day it was registered: the cheapest observation this class was registered to await was taken, and it went against the premise... This closes the class.' (2) RET — doc §3.3 (lines 213-214) lists it unqualified among 'Kinase leads with EMC-specific evidence that nobody followed.' MOD-RET verdict='excluded', rationale: 'RE-GRADED 2026-08-09 on EVIDENCE QUALITY... the activation claim is a single sentence in a paywalled abstract, about a limited set of at most ten tumours, with no recoverable denominator.' (Doc §3.8's own grading table softens this to 'split', not 'excluded' — the two sections of the same document disagree with each other about this class's status.) (3) ALK/ROS1 — doc §3.3 (lines 219-221) lists it as a live kinase lead awaiting a 'first step'. MOD-ALK-ROS1 verdict='excluded', rationale: '⛔ RE-GRADED 2026-08-09 by reading the screen the class was raised from... two of its three hits belong to a DIFFERENT single class, which is already on the board... unattributable here in principle' — i.e. the 'first step' the manuscript frames as still to be taken was already taken and returned a closure. (4) Matrix (glycosaminoglycan) biosynthesis — doc §3.4 (lines 233-237): 'the third option is to stop the tumour building it... the relevant expression read is already committed here and has never been graded for this purpose.' MOD-CS-BIOSYNTHESIS verdict='excluded', rationale: 'RE-GRADED 2026-08-09... This closes the class.' Doc §3.8's own table (line 298) confirms the grading happened and reports it: 'matrix biosynthesis | against as stated — the sulfate-donor module is lower, not higher, than in comparator sarcomas.' §3.4 and §3.8 of the SAME document contradict each other about whether this class has been graded. (5) Treatment sequencing — doc §3.6 (line 264) lists 'sequencing' among the live strategy classes. MOD-SEQUENCING verdict='excluded', rationale: 'RE-GRADED 2026-08-09 on EVIDENCE BASE... this closes the class as an analysis target while making the negative itself publishable.' (6) Hormone-responsive 5′-partner lane (SERM/SERD) — doc §3.7 (lines 276-278) presents it as live: 'a hormone-responsive 5′ partner can import a druggable transcriptional input the driver does not otherwise have, and there is a reported instance of exactly that with durable benefit.' MOD-SERM-SERD verdict='excluded', rationale: 'RE-GRADED 2026-08-09 on REACH... one is reported in a single EMC patient in the world literature and in none of the partner-genotyped cases the cited cohorts cover... what fails is the number of patients it could reach, which for an ultra-rare disease is the whole question.'
blockers.fix: Re-run §3.1, §3.3, §3.4, §3.6 and §3.7 against the current systems/graph/modalities.json verdicts before this paper is hardened further. Either (a) move these six classes into §4's closed-shapes accounting and state their closure rationale there, or (b) if the intent is to narrate the state at first registration and separately show the same-day re-grading, say so explicitly in each subsection rather than leaving §3's prose reading as current status. Either way, §3.4 and §3.8 cannot continue to assert opposite things about whether the matrix-biosynthesis class has been graded.

p1s.summary: The phrase 'a reported instance of exactly that with durable benefit' (§3.7) sits close to the efficacy language the document's own headline caveat forbids ('Nothing here asserts efficacy, safety, a therapeutic window or clinical readiness — for any class, in any verdict, including the ones that survive'), and it describes the one class in the census that is both n=1-patient-in-the-world-literature and already excluded on reach grounds per MOD-SERM-SERD. As currently worded a reader cannot tell that from the sentence.
p1s.evidence: Line 278: 'there is a reported instance of exactly that with durable benefit.' Compare MOD-SERM-SERD rationale: 'one is reported in a single EMC patient in the world literature and in none of the partner-genotyped cases the cited cohorts cover' and verdict='excluded'.
p1s.fix: If §3.7 is retained after the blocker fix above, qualify the sentence with the n=1 and the reach-based exclusion in the same breath, rather than only naming 'durable benefit'.

p1s.summary: Nothing in the repository currently prevents the manuscript's hand-typed §2 summary table from drifting from systems/graph/modalities.json a second time — the same failure mode §2.1 already documents once (the 127→112 correction) has now recurred in the opposite direction (31 candidates claimed vs. 20 actual) without being caught before this review.
p1s.evidence: §2.1 already narrates one prior correction of this exact table for a different reason (false `never_searched` positives). The blocker above shows a second, larger drift in the verdict distribution itself was never caught.
p1s.fix: Generate §2's table (and the '31'/'84' figures repeated in §3/§4) programmatically from systems/graph/modalities.json at manuscript-build time, per CLAUDE.md §1 ('a total is DERIVED, never typed'), rather than re-typing it by hand each time the graph is re-graded.
